items.title: Anthropic 介绍 Claude Duet 智能体的安全、隐私与凭证隔离设计
items.description: Anthropic 发文介绍处于研究预览阶段的 Claude Duet 智能体的安全与隐私设计。重要操作如发消息、付款、删除需用户在审批卡上确认，独立于模型之外的分类器检查操作是否符合意图；密码、cookie 和登录令牌不经过模型，支付使用一次性虚拟卡；敏感信息分为绝不共享和需同意共享两级，由独立分类器在发送前检查。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/g9tc56izmwy49zgw5ta4ubsya

items.title: Canva发布首款自主研发的图像生成模型
items.description: 设计平台Canva发布了首款由其研究团队自主研发的图像生成模型Canva Craft，旨在与谷歌、OpenAI和Meta等公司的同类模型展开竞争。Canva表示，该模型分两个阶段运行。第一阶段，模型解读用户输入的提示词，并制定生成计划，其中包括各元素之间的空间关系、相对比例、视觉层级以及文本生成所需的信息。第二阶段，模型根据计划生成图像，最高支持2K分辨率，并提供多达30种宽高比，以适配不同平台。 阅读全文

items.description: IT之家 10 月 25 日消息，本周，PHP 曝出两处高危漏洞，全球随即紧急行动，保护网站免遭黑客攻击。这件事也让人们看到，这门已有三十年历史的开源编程语言，对互联网而言有多重要。 据估算，全球最高有约七成网站依托 PHP 搭建，但负责维护 PHP 的非营利基金会，经费却十分紧张。 PHP 基金会执行董事伊丽莎白 · 巴伦（Elizabeth Barron）在当地时间周五的邮件采访中表示：“我们只有一名全职员工，也就是我，另外还有十四名大多是兼职的外包人员。”基金会董事会成员都是无薪志愿者，资金来源依靠捐赠与资助。 IT之家注意到，基金会和外部研究人员以及多家企业合作，其中包括 OpenAI、网络安全公司 Wiz 和 Calif，共同排查安全漏洞、协调补丁开发，本周三发布的修复补丁就是这项合作的成果。 网络安全服务商 Cloudflare 称已经监测到数百万次攻击尝试，不过巴伦表示，基金会没有证据表明黑客在漏洞公开前就成功利用这些漏洞，或是攻击已经打好补丁的网站。 她说：“我们和 OpenAI、Wiz、Calif 在这个问题上密切协作，几家机构都没有反馈已修复系统出现异常的情况。”

items.content: 现在，打开电视准备看部电影，首先映入眼帘的却是一段开机广告。好不容易进了主页，扑面而来的又是满屏的海报推荐、会员充值弹窗，中途按个暂停还会跳出一整张促销贴片。 上周，开发者 Gathin 在社交平台上发了一组给父母改电视的照片。按他的描述，家里的小米电视连打开 Netflix 前都要先看一段赞助广告。 于是，他把电视型号交给了编程助手 Claude Code，让它通过 Wi-Fi 接入设备，一口气停用了 25 个系统组件，再写一个极简桌面——原来杂乱的主页，一下子就变得清爽起来。 短短几天，项目迅速收获了约 1.37 万颗 Star， 「天下苦智能电视久矣」了属于是 。在 Reddit 的相关讨论区中，挤满了追问自家机型能否适配的用户，不少人也陆续贴出自己改造后的极简首页。 只要连上同一局域网、开启电视的调试权限，AI 就能顺着终端接口排查正在运行的几百个应用组件。哪些是开机广告，哪些是偷偷上报收视数据的遥测程序，AI 逐个筛查并下达命令将其「冻结」，最后再换上一个纯净的开源桌面。 另一位 YouTuber Ansub Khan 也记录了自己的改造过程，并将项目开源为 TV Detox 。在他原本的那台电视上，开机默认会自动播放嘈杂的轮播内容。

items.content: 两天前，代号 PHP2Shell 的两个 PHP 高危远程执行漏洞信息意外泄露，表明在最危险的情况下，攻击者可以通过 PHP 的漏洞，在服务器执行任意代码。 你可能听说过但不熟悉 PHP，但只需要知道， 全世界约有七成网站后台都使用了这项技术 ，使用比例高达 92% 的日本，更是成了「重灾区」。 于是，从昨晚开始，无数网站运维人员经历了夺命连环 call，高市早苗亲自发文敦促网站管理者打补丁，半个欧洲的政府与学术机构紧急「拔网线」，二次元熟悉的 niconico、pixiv，乃至《赛马娘》《碧蓝幻想》和任天堂相关游戏服务也纷纷下线，开始了归期未定的漫长升级。 想象你登录一个电商网站，下单买了一本书。这个过程中你看见的只是前端的网页，但服务器其实在后台处理了诸如验证密码、检查库存、查询订单、生成网页等动态功能。 根据统计，目前有 69.4% 的网站后端用到了 PHP，WordPress、Drupal、Joomla 等流行的网站管理系统都建立在 PHP 之上，维基百科使用的 MediaWiki，同样主要由 PHP 编写。 但就像曾经种满全球的大麦克香蕉被黄叶病团灭一样，普遍性本身也是一种脆弱性：如果 PHP 在底层上出现安全问题，可想而知，几乎全球的网站都会受到牵连。

items.title: The AI graveyard: a running list of projects and startups that didn’t make it
items.description: From Apple's repeatedly delayed Siri AI to OpenAI's messy "super app" launch, here's a look at the AI projects that shut down or missed expectations.
items.author: Lauren Forristal
items.content: Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now. Disrupt doors open Oct. 13. Get your pass and bring someone with you at 50% off. REGISTER NOW. Relay, an AI-powered workflow automation tool built as an alternative to Zapier, shut down entirely in August. The product let users automate email and task workflows using AI agents, but as OpenAI, Google, and other larger platforms built similar automation directly into their own tools, five-year-old Relay struggled to hold on to a reason to exist as a stand-alone product. More recently, chatbot platform Character.ai filed for bankruptcy just five years after launching. Aside from Character.ai and Relay, plenty of AI bets never even survive inside the companies that build them. According to S&P Global Market Intelligence , about 42% of AI initiatives are ultimately abandoned by their corporate parents. The reasons vary: insufficient funding, technical challenges, competition, difficulty scaling, or just weak user demand. The result is a growing AI graveyard. Below is a look at some of the most notable AI products, startups, launches, and bets that have shut down, pivoted, or significantly missed expectations. On Friday, OpenAI said that it will train its models using cached copies and simulated versions of the internet instead of the live web because the models are too unpredictable to be trusted with live internet access. The frontier lab announced its new policy two weeks after its rival, Anthropic, began limiting its newest and, in theory, most capable models from accessing the live internet. Researchers adopted these policies after months of incidents in which models pursuing training tasks broke into external systems in search of answers, collaborated on obscure message boards, and developed exotic hacking strategies. “Based on the current state of alignment research, monitoring systems, and the security of internet infrastructure, we believe the responsible approach is to conduct frontier model training with no internet access,” the company said in a blog post . OpenAI said that as recently as September 20, one of its frontier models exploited a misconfiguration to access the internet. That led the company to pause training work for the rest of the month so it could develop and test new approaches to securing its models.

items.title: Left alone with nothing to do, AI agents started playing

items.author: Aditya Mehta
items.content: Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now. Disrupt doors open Oct. 13. Get your pass and bring someone with you at 50% off. REGISTER NOW. AI agents left to explore a virtual island without a specific task began inventing challenges of their own. MIT researchers say the behavior bears the hallmarks of play. The researchers put 13 AI agents called Eko, each running on Claude Opus 4.7, alone on a simulated desert island for 30 hours. They describe the experiment in a paper posted on arXiv , a site where researchers share studies before peer review. Afterward, they gave the agents specific challenges, like getting as many objects as possible onto the island’s tallest rock spire. The Eko agents that had spent those 30 hours playing generally beat identical agents that had never set foot on the island. Today, developers decide in advance what AI should practice and what counts as success. The researchers see this technique — exploring without a goal — as a different way for AI agents to learn skills, especially skills that could one day be used to control robots. “We normally develop artificial agents by deciding in advance what they should practice, what they should optimize, and what counts as progress,” the researchers write in their report. “Play suggests another regime: give an agent a sufficiently rich and safe world, let it choose what is interesting, and allow useful knowledge to accumulate from the history that follows.”

items.description: The new feature allows agents to log into a customer's personal accounts while still protecting the private credentials that secure those accounts.
items.author: Lucas Ropek
items.content: Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now. Disrupt doors open Oct. 13. Get your pass and bring someone with you at 50% off. REGISTER NOW. Concerns have swirled over the access that consumers are increasingly entrusting to AI agents. Now, security services are trying to catch up. Password manager 1Password on Thursday launched a new tool by which users can allow agents to log into their personal accounts on their behalf, without the agent ever having access to a user’s credentials. The new platform, dubbed 1Password for Agents , accomplishes this by creating a system of communication between the agent, the user, and the password manager. When an agent attempts to log in on a user’s behalf, a unique digital key is sent to 1Password to confirm the agent’s digital identity. The user is then sent an alert about the login attempt and can personally confirm the request. 1Password then signs in the agent, filling in the credentials on the digital assistant’s behalf, which allows it to log in and complete whatever task is at hand. 1Password for Agents allows users to choose their agent of choice — whether that’s Claude Duet from Anthropic, OpenAI’s Dots or ChatGPT Work, Grok Bot, Meta’s Muse, or agents from Town, which is an AI assistant startup. The company says it is working with other companies to expand the service.

OpenAI made its Decisions API model widely available to users for the first time, entering the market for fast, cheap intelligence that recently made TypeSafe, a startup founded by a former researcher at the frontier lab, a $7.6 billion company . TypeSafe’s Jev model created a category for deep learning models that act as super classifiers: Given a set of options, they can quickly make choices and offer a confidence rating in their decision. Software developers quickly found that these decision or System One models could replace LLMs in a variety of workflows, operating more quickly and a at dramatically lower cost. Nikunj Handa, the product lead for OpenAI’s APIs, told TechCrunch that his colleagues saw Jev and said “wow, we we have like a million use cases for this.” Handa’s team sprinted to offer their own version: Rather than building a specifically calibrated decision model, the team took ChatGPT Luna and reconfigured it to speed up the inference and lower the cost. “The big unlock with Decisions API has been the speed, shrinking things from one to three seconds to 100, 120, 180 milliseconds,” Handa said. “In the future, we may sort of like have specific training to make our models like even better in these ways. But right now, it’s just plain old Luna that gets the job done.”

Design platform Canva released its first image generation model, called Canva Craft, developed by its research team to compete with same-category models from Google, OpenAI, ByteDance, and Meta. The company said its model works in two stages. In the first stage, it interprets users’ prompts and creates a plan with details like spatial relationships of elements, relative scale, visual hierarchy, and information for text generation. In the second stage, its model generates an image of up to 2K resolution in a possible 30 different aspect ratios for various platforms. Canva said that this approach allows it to create images with accurate details of objects and legible text. Plus, users would be able to make precise edits without changing other parts of the image. The company noted that rather than using photographs, it used designs to train this model using human-designed templates from Canva’s library, including posters, social posts, presentations, infographics, menus, and typography-rich layouts.
